contentObjective: I can determine the mean of a data set, use a target mean to find a missing value, and explain the mean as the fair share and the balance point of the data.
languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words mean, average, measure of center, balance point, and data set.

vocabulary.definition: The average of a data set. Add all the values, then divide by how many values there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio de un conjunto de datos. Suma todos los valores y divide entre cuántos valores hay.
vocabulary.visual: Miguel earned $60 in 4 days: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so the mean is $15 per day.
vocabulary.cloze: The value found by adding all the data and dividing by how many values there are is the ___.

examples.why: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.
That is the total; the mean still needs the division.

vocabulary.definition: Another word for the mean — the amount each value would be if the total were shared equally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Otra palabra para la media: la cantidad que tendría cada valor si el total se repartiera en partes iguales.
vocabulary.visual: A player averages 15 points per game, so over 10 games she scores 15 × 10 = 150 points in all.
vocabulary.cloze: A common everyday word that means the same thing as the mean is the ___.

examples.why: That is the total before sharing.

vocabulary.definition: A single number used to describe the middle, or typical value, of a whole data set.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un solo número que se usa para describir el centro, o valor típico, de todo un conjunto de datos.
vocabulary.visual: The mean, $15, is one measure of center that describes all four of Miguel's days at once.
vocabulary.cloze: A single number that describes the typical value of a whole data set is a ___.

examples.why: One number standing for the typical value.

vocabulary.definition: The value where the total distance of the data above it equals the total distance below it. The mean is the balance point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El valor donde la distancia total de los datos por encima es igual a la distancia total por debajo. La media es el punto de equilibrio.
vocabulary.visual: With a target mean of 15, points totaling 13 below must be matched by points totaling 13 above.
vocabulary.cloze: The value where the total amount above equals the total amount below is the ___.

examples.why: Distances above and below it cancel out.
Everything sits below it, so nothing balances.

vocabulary.definition: The whole collection of values that were gathered or measured.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Toda la colección de valores que se recopilaron o midieron.
vocabulary.visual: Sofia's points in games 1–9 — 12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, 10, 18 — form one data set.
vocabulary.cloze: The whole collection of collected values is the ___.

examples.why: The whole collection that was gathered.
One value is a member, not the set.

copyPanel.formula: Mean = (Sum of all values) ÷ (Total number of values)
steps: 1. Add all data values together to find the total sum
2. Divide the sum by the count of data values
3. Concept: The mean represents the fair share or balance point of the data

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Honor Roll
revealWordProblem.text:
Shanice wants to be on the honor roll for the next marking period. She works out that her mean test score has to be at least 90 in both math and science. Her test scores so far this grading period are shown in her student portal.
Question: How likely is it that Shanice will make the honor roll? Explain what she still has to do.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A student portal screen showing recent test scores: math scores 88, 82, 92, and 95, and science scores 95, 85, and 88.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Math so far: 88 + 82 + 92 + 95 = 357, a mean of 89.25. With one more test the mean is (357 + x) ÷ 5, and that is at least 90 when 357 + x ≥ 450, so x ≥ 93. Science so far: 95 + 85 + 88 = 268, a mean of about 89.3. With one more test the mean is (268 + x) ÷ 4, and that is at least 90 when 268 + x ≥ 360, so x ≥ 92. Shanice needs at least 93 in math and 92 in science. She has already scored 92 and 95 in math and 95 in science, so it is possible — but she has no room to slip.

questions.explanation: Add the values: 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 28. There are 4 values, so the mean is 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
choiceFeedback: 28 is the total of the four values, not the mean — you still have to divide that total by 4.
8 is one of the values in the list, but the mean is the leveled amount for all four, found by dividing the total by 4.
6 is another value from the list; picking a value from the data is not the same as adding and dividing.
hints: The mean is what each value would be if the total were shared out equally among all four numbers.
Mean = total ÷ how many values. Count first: there are 4 values here.
Step 1: add 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 to get the total. Step 2: divide that total by 4.
questions.explanationEs: Suma los valores: 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 28. Hay 4 valores, así que la media es 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
hintsEs: La media es lo que tendría cada valor si el total se repartiera en partes iguales entre los cuatro números.
Media = total ÷ cuántos valores hay. Cuenta primero: aquí hay 4 valores.
Paso 1: suma 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 para obtener el total. Paso 2: divide ese total entre 4.

questions.stem: Miguel earned $60 walking dogs over 4 days. What is his mean daily earning?
questions.explanation: The total is $60 and there are 4 days, so the mean is 60 ÷ 4 = $15 per day.
choiceFeedback: $60 is the total for all 4 days combined — a typical single day must be much smaller than the whole week's total.
$4 is the number of days, not an amount of money; the days are what you divide BY.
$20 comes from dividing 60 by 3 instead of 4 — count the days again.
hints: A typical day is the amount Miguel would earn if he earned the SAME amount all 4 days.
You already know the total, so only one step is left: split that total equally among the days.
Divide the $60 total by the 4 days to find the equal share for one day.
questions.stemEs: Miguel ganó $60 paseando perros durante 4 días. ¿Cuál es su ganancia media diaria?
questions.explanationEs: El total es $60 y hay 4 días, así que la media es 60 ÷ 4 = $15 por día.
hintsEs: Un día típico es la cantidad que Miguel ganaría si ganara LO MISMO los 4 días.
Ya conoces el total, así que solo falta un paso: repartir ese total en partes iguales entre los días.
Divide el total de $60 entre los 4 días para hallar la parte igual de un día.

questions.explanation: Add the values: 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 35. There are 5 values, so the mean is 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
choiceFeedback: 35 is the sum of the five values — the mean requires the second step of dividing that sum by 5.
9 is the fourth value in the list, not the leveled value for all five numbers.
5 is how many values there are, not the mean; that count is the divisor, not the answer.
hints: Mean means average: level all five numbers out so they are all the same.
Find the total of all five numbers first, then divide by the number of values, 5.
Step 1: add 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11. Step 2: divide that total by 5.
questions.explanationEs: Suma los valores: 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 35. Hay 5 valores, así que la media es 35 ÷ 5 = 7.
hintsEs: Media significa promedio: nivela los cinco números para que todos sean iguales.
Halla primero el total de los cinco números y luego divide entre la cantidad de valores, 5.
Paso 1: suma 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11. Paso 2: divide ese total entre 5.

reviewHighlights.formula: Mean = (Sum of all values) ÷ (Total number of values)
steps: 1. Add all data values together to find the total sum
2. Divide the sum by the count of data values
3. Concept: The mean represents the fair share or balance point of the data
reviewHighlights.watchOut: The most common mistake with the mean is adding correctly and then dividing by the wrong number — or not dividing at all. Students report the total (for 8, 10, 6, 12 they say the mean is 36) or they divide by a count that does not match the data, such as dividing a 4-value total by 5, or skipping a zero when counting the values. Before you finish, do two things: count the values in the data set out loud, and check that your mean lands between the smallest and largest value. A mean of 36 for data that never goes above 12 is impossible.

level1.stem: In her first 4 games, Sofia scored 12, 20, 16, and 11 points. What is her mean points per game so far?
level1.explanation: Add the points: 12 + 20 + 16 + 11 = 59. There are 4 games, so the mean is 59 ÷ 4 = 14.75 points per game.
choiceFeedback: 59 is her total points across the 4 games, not her per-game average — divide that total by 4.
15 is Sofia's TARGET mean, not what she has actually averaged so far; compute the mean from her real scores.
20 is her single best game, and one high game is not the average of all four.
hints: The mean here answers: how many points per game has Sofia averaged so far?
Add up the four game scores, then divide the total by the number of games played, 4.
Step 1: add 12 + 20 + 16 + 11. Step 2: divide that total by 4 — the answer will not be a whole number.
level1.stemEs: En sus primeros 4 juegos, Sofía anotó 12, 20, 16 y 11 puntos. ¿Cuál es su media de puntos por juego hasta ahora?
level1.explanationEs: Suma los puntos: 12 + 20 + 16 + 11 = 59. Hay 4 juegos, así que la media es 59 ÷ 4 = 14.75 puntos por juego.
hintsEs: La media aquí responde: ¿cuántos puntos por juego ha promediado Sofía hasta ahora?
Suma los cuatro puntajes y luego divide el total entre la cantidad de juegos, 4.
Paso 1: suma 12 + 20 + 16 + 11. Paso 2: divide ese total entre 4; la respuesta no será un número entero.

level2.stem: Sofia wants to average 15 points per game over 10 games. How many points does she need in all 10 games combined?
level2.explanation: If every one of the 10 games hit the target of 15 points, the total would be 15 × 10 = 150 points. That is the total she needs for a mean of 15.
choiceFeedback: 15 is the mean for ONE game, but the question asks for all 10 games combined.
25 comes from adding 15 and 10 instead of multiplying them; the total is a mean repeated once per game.
1.5 comes from dividing 15 by 10, but dividing makes the total smaller than one game, which cannot be right.
hints: Undo the mean: the mean was found by dividing a total by the count, so the total comes back by doing the opposite.
Imagine every one of the 10 games landed exactly on 15 points. What would the season total be?
Use 15 points per game, ten times over.
level2.stemEs: Sofía quiere promediar 15 puntos por juego en 10 juegos. ¿Cuántos puntos necesita en total en los 10 juegos?
level2.explanationEs: Si cada uno de los 10 juegos alcanzara el objetivo de 15 puntos, el total sería 15 × 10 = 150 puntos. Ese es el total que necesita para una media de 15.
hintsEs: Deshaz la media: la media se obtuvo dividiendo un total entre la cantidad, así que el total vuelve haciendo lo contrario.
Imagina que cada uno de los 10 juegos cayera exactamente en 15 puntos. ¿Cuál sería el total de la temporada?
Usa 15 puntos por juego, diez veces.

level2.stem: Sofia's points in games 1 through 9 were 12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, 10, and 18. How many points has she scored so far?

15 is her target mean per game, not a season total across nine games.
hints: This step asks only for a total — no dividing yet.
Add the nine scores in small groups so you can check yourself, for example three games at a time.
Try 12 + 20 + 16 = 48, then 11 + 17 + 14 = 42, then 15 + 10 + 18 = 43, and combine those three subtotals.
level2.stemEs: Los puntos de Sofía en los juegos 1 al 9 fueron 12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, 10 y 18. ¿Cuántos puntos ha anotado hasta ahora?
hintsEs: Este paso pide solo un total: todavía no hay que dividir.
Suma los nueve puntajes en grupos pequeños para poder comprobarte, por ejemplo de tres en tres.

level2.stem: Sofia has 133 points after 9 games and needs 150 points in all to average 15 over 10 games. How many points must she score in game 10?
level2.explanation: She needs 150 points in all and already has 133, so game 10 must supply 150 − 133 = 17 points.
choiceFeedback: 15 is the target mean itself; that would only work if her first 9 games had already averaged exactly 15.
13 is how many points she sits BELOW the needed total in a different comparison — subtract 133 from 150 carefully.
283 comes from adding 150 and 133; the last game supplies the missing part of the total, so you subtract.
hints: You know the total she needs and the total she already has — the last game covers the gap between them.
Decide whether the gap is found by adding or by subtracting the two totals.
Subtract her current 133 points from the 150 points she needs.
level2.stemEs: Sofía tiene 133 puntos después de 9 juegos y necesita 150 puntos en total para promediar 15 en 10 juegos. ¿Cuántos puntos debe anotar en el juego 10?
level2.explanationEs: Necesita 150 puntos en total y ya tiene 133, así que el juego 10 debe aportar 150 − 133 = 17 puntos.
hintsEs: Conoces el total que necesita y el total que ya tiene: el último juego cubre la diferencia entre ambos.
Decide si esa diferencia se halla sumando o restando los dos totales.
Resta sus 133 puntos actuales de los 150 puntos que necesita.

level2.prompt: Sofia realized she made an error: she actually scored 12 points in Game 8, not 10. Her other games are unchanged (12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15, and 18). How does this change the number of points she needs in Game 10 to average 15 points per game? Show how you know.
level2.promptEs: Sofía se dio cuenta de un error: en realidad anotó 12 puntos en el Juego 8, no 10. Sus otros juegos no cambian (12, 20, 16, 11, 17, 14, 15 y 18). ¿Cómo cambia esto los puntos que necesita en el Juego 10 para promediar 15 puntos por juego? Muestra cómo lo sabes.
level2.sentenceFrame: Her new total after 9 games is ___ points. To average 15 over 10 games she still needs ___ points in all, so Game 10 must now be ___ points. That is ___ points fewer than before, because ___.
hints: Only one value changed, so you do not have to re-add everything from scratch.
Decide first how much the 9-game total moved, then compare that new total to the 150 points she still needs.
The old 9-game total was 133 and Game 8 went up by 2. Update the total, then subtract it from 150.
hintsEs: Solo cambió un valor, así que no tienes que volver a sumar todo desde cero.
Decide primero cuánto se movió el total de 9 juegos y luego compara ese nuevo total con los 150 puntos que aún necesita.
El total anterior de 9 juegos era 133 y el Juego 8 subió 2. Actualiza el total y luego réstalo de 150.
level2.explanation: Raising Game 8 from 10 to 12 adds 2 points, so the 9-game total goes from 133 to 135. The target has not changed: a mean of 15 over 10 games still needs 15 × 10 = 150 points in all. So Game 10 must now supply 150 − 135 = 15 points instead of 17 — exactly 2 fewer, because every point gained earlier is a point she no longer has to score later.
level2.explanationEs: Subir el Juego 8 de 10 a 12 agrega 2 puntos, así que el total de 9 juegos pasa de 133 a 135. El objetivo no cambia: una media de 15 en 10 juegos sigue necesitando 15 × 10 = 150 puntos en total. Así que el Juego 10 debe aportar ahora 150 − 135 = 15 puntos en vez de 17, exactamente 2 menos, porque cada punto ganado antes es un punto que ya no tiene que anotar después.

level3.stem: A data set has a mean of 20. Every value in the data set is then increased by 4. What is the new mean?
level3.explanation: If every value moves up by 4, the balance point moves up by 4 as well, so the new mean is 20 + 4 = 24. In totals: adding 4 to each of n values adds 4n to the total, and 4n ÷ n = 4.
choiceFeedback: 20 would be right only if the values did not move, but every single value shifted up by 4.
80 comes from multiplying the mean by 4, but the values were increased by 4, not multiplied by 4.
5 comes from dividing 20 by 4; the change was an addition to each value, so the mean changes by addition too.
hints: Picture the mean as a balance point and every data value sliding 4 units to the right.
If the whole data set shifts by the same amount, does the center shift too, or stay put?
Try a tiny example: 18, 20, 22 has a mean of 20. Add 4 to each value and find the new mean.
level3.stemEs: Un conjunto de datos tiene una media de 20. Luego cada valor del conjunto aumenta en 4. ¿Cuál es la nueva media?
level3.explanationEs: Si cada valor sube 4, el punto de equilibrio también sube 4, así que la nueva media es 20 + 4 = 24. En totales: sumar 4 a cada uno de los n valores agrega 4n al total, y 4n ÷ n = 4.
hintsEs: Imagina la media como un punto de equilibrio y cada valor deslizándose 4 unidades a la derecha.
Si todo el conjunto se desplaza la misma cantidad, ¿el centro también se desplaza o se queda igual?
Prueba un ejemplo pequeño: 18, 20, 22 tiene media 20. Suma 4 a cada valor y halla la nueva media.

level3.stem: A data set of 5 numbers has a mean of 12. A sixth value of 12 is added. What happens to the mean?
choices: It stays 12 — adding a value equal to the mean cannot pull it either way
It rises, because the total went up
It falls, because there are more values to divide by
There is not enough information without the original five numbers
level3.explanation: Five numbers with a mean of 12 add up to 60. Adding one more 12 makes the total 72. There are 6 values now, so divide: 72 ÷ 6 = 12. Adding a value equal to the mean never moves the mean.
choiceFeedback: The total did rise — but so did the count, and by a matching amount.
More values lower the mean only if the new value sits below it.
The mean and the count are enough; the individual values do not matter here.
hints: What is the total of five numbers with a mean of 12?
Add 12 to that total and divide by the new count.
Compare your answer with 12.
level3.stemEs: Un conjunto de 5 números tiene una media de 12. Se agrega un sexto valor de 12. ¿Qué le pasa a la media?
choicesEs: Se queda en 12 — agregar un valor igual a la media no puede moverla
Baja, porque hay más valores entre los que dividir
No hay información suficiente sin los cinco números originales
level3.explanationEs: Cinco números con una media de 12 suman 60. Al añadir otro 12, el total es 72. Ahora hay 6 valores, así que divide: 72 ÷ 6 = 12. Añadir un valor igual a la media nunca mueve la media.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el total de cinco números con media 12?
Suma 12 a ese total y divide entre el nuevo conteo.
Compara tu resultado con 12.

level3.stem: Miguel earned $60 walking dogs over 4 days. Ana says his mean daily earning is $15. Beto says you cannot know, because Miguel might have earned nothing on some days. Who is right?
choices: Ana — the mean spreads the total evenly and does not claim he earned $15 each day
Beto — a mean is meaningless when the daily amounts are unknown
Both — the mean is $15 but it is not a useful number
level3.explanation: The mean shares the total evenly across the days. Miguel earned $60 over 4 days, so divide: 60 ÷ 4 = 15. The mean does not claim he earned $15 on every single day. Beto is right about the real days, but Ana answered the question that was asked.
choiceFeedback: The mean is defined from the total and the count, both of which are known.
It is useful — it is the fair share, which is what the question asks for.
That multiplies instead of dividing: 60 × 4.
hints: What does the mean describe — each actual day, or an even share?
Do you need the individual days to compute 60 ÷ 4?
Which of the two students answered the question that was asked?
level3.stemEs: Miguel ganó $60 paseando perros durante 4 días. Ana dice que su ganancia diaria media es $15. Beto dice que no se puede saber, porque Miguel pudo no ganar nada algunos días. ¿Quién tiene razón?
choicesEs: Ana — la media reparte el total por igual y no afirma que ganó $15 cada día
Beto — una media no tiene sentido cuando se desconocen las cantidades diarias
Los dos — la media es $15 pero no es un número útil
level3.explanationEs: La media reparte el total en partes iguales entre los días. Miguel ganó $60 en 4 días, así que divide: 60 ÷ 4 = 15. La media no afirma que ganó $15 cada día. Beto tiene razón sobre los días reales, pero Ana respondió la pregunta que se hizo.
hintsEs: ¿Qué describe la media — cada día real o un reparto igualado?
¿Necesitas los días individuales para calcular 60 ÷ 4?
¿Cuál de los dos respondió la pregunta que se hizo?

level3.stem: Claim: “The mean is always one of the values in the data set.” Always, sometimes, or never true?
choices: Sometimes — 3, 5, 7 has a mean of 5, but 4, 6, 8, 10 has a mean of 7, which is not in the set
Always — the mean has to come from the data
Never — the mean is a calculation, so it cannot match a value
Sometimes — it depends whether the count of values is odd
level3.explanation: The mean is a balance point, not always a member of the list. Find the mean of 3, 5, 7: it is 5, and 5 is in the set. Now find the mean of 4, 6, 8, 10: it is 7, and 7 is not. One example each way makes the claim sometimes true.
choiceFeedback: It is computed from the data, which is not the same as being in it.
It can match — 3, 5, 7 has a mean of 5.
Try 4, 6, 8, 10 with an even count and 1, 2, 30 with an odd one; the count is not what decides it.
hints: Find the mean of 3, 5, 7. Is it in the list?
Now find the mean of 4, 6, 8, 10. Is that one in the list?
One example each way settles the claim.
level3.stemEs: Afirmación: “La media siempre es uno de los valores del conjunto de datos.” ¿Siempre, a veces o nunca es cierto?
choicesEs: A veces — 3, 5, 7 tiene media 5, pero 4, 6, 8, 10 tiene media 7, que no está en el conjunto
Siempre — la media tiene que venir de los datos
Nunca — la media es un cálculo, así que no puede coincidir con un valor
A veces — depende de si la cantidad de valores es impar
level3.explanationEs: La media es un punto de equilibrio, no siempre un miembro de la lista. Halla la media de 3, 5, 7: es 5, y 5 sí está en el conjunto. Ahora halla la media de 4, 6, 8, 10: es 7, y 7 no está. Un ejemplo de cada tipo hace que la afirmación sea a veces verdadera.
hintsEs: Halla la media de 3, 5, 7. ¿Está en la lista?
Ahora halla la media de 4, 6, 8, 10. ¿Está esa en la lista?
Un ejemplo de cada tipo resuelve la afirmación.
